summary: CADCraft v0.10.0 (pre-alpha, pure Rust) has a solid, tested xref core (XATTACH/-XREF/XBIND/XOPEN/palette, overlays, relative paths, nested+circular bounds, host-side layer overrides persisted in DXF and DWG) and a deliberate stored-path security policy via the craft-docpath crate (only local files or the drawing's own network share are followed; other computers, devices and URLs are refused with a status, never an error). Data connections are thin: table data links read CSV only, carried as CADCraft xdata (invisible to AutoCAD), no fields/hyperlinks/Excel/DB. File containment is folder-shaped: no project container, eTransmit, sheet sets, .bak, or change notification; copy between drawings (clipboard, INSERT from file, IMPORT) uses one deterministic merge rule (existing target definitions win, anonymous blocks renamed, new handles, associativity dropped) but WBLOCK copies the whole symbol table and writes non-atomically. Crash safety is the strongest area: clippy deny of unwrap/expect/panic, forbid(unsafe), catch_unwind at every boundary with restore from a cheap Arc<Drawing> snapshot (made cheap by a copy-on-write chunked entity store), non-finite result refusal, 100 test functions named hostile across 2,110 tests (recounted 2026-10-21), caps on every input-sized loop, background autosave with lock files and immediate autosave on GPU faults, AUDIT/RECOVER. Weak spots the docs admit: no CI gate on PRs (stability scored 35%), no web autosave, DWG via acadrust->DXF-text bridge with a 6x inflation and the #57 10 MB DWG failure (throughput still open), DWG save drops unmodelled data, no XCLIP or in-place xref editing, Unloaded xref state lost on reopen.

unique_strengths: craft-docpath stored-path policy: xref and data-link paths saved in a drawing are followed only on this computer or the drawing's own network share; other computers, device paths and URLs become an 'Unresolved' status with a reason instead of being opened (AutoCAD has no equivalent)

Every xref failure (missing, refused, unreadable, too big, circular, too deep) leaves an empty block with a status; the host always opens and the reference survives a save; bare file name beside the host is tried as a fallback for relocated projects
Host-side xref layer overrides persist through both DXF and DWG save/reopen, verified by a test (#886)

Copy-on-write chunked entity store makes every undo step, pre-command snapshot, autosave and clipboard definition set an O(1) pointer copy, which is what makes panic-restore and background autosave free

Layered panic containment (execute, interactive step, prompt/preview, open, DWG bridge, LISP, render thread) plus non-finite-result refusal, enforced by clippy deny lints and 100 test functions named hostile (2,110 tests total; recounted 2026-10-21)

Autosave design: per-instance file names, lock-file heartbeat so concurrent apps don't offer each other's files, only self-named files ever deleted, immediate autosave on GPU error/device loss, retry after failed write
Content-identity-keyed R-tree cache that cannot go stale regardless of edit path; 200k-entity pick in 0.001 ms (internal numbers)
Everything is a command: xrefs, data links, recovery and audit are all reachable from MCP, a JSON control channel, the CLI and AutoLISP
notable_weaknesses: No project container: no eTransmit/archive, Sheet Set Manager, Reference Manager, manifest, .bak backup, or recorded found-at/hash/mtime per reference (gaps F23, 40-70 h)
No xref change detection: no file watcher, no 'needs reload' notice; every Reload re-reads and re-imports the whole file; xref loading after OPEN is synchronous
Unloaded xref state is lost on reopen (xref_status not serialised); no XCLIP, no in-place xref editing, no demand loading, no PDF/image underlays
Data links are CSV read-only, 8 MiB, stored as CADCraft xdata (invisible to AutoCAD, lost through DWG); no fields, hyperlinks, Excel or database connections

DWG is an acadrust->DXF-text bridge with ~6x inflation; issue #57 (9.9 MB DWG, ~2 min, 1.1 GB RAM, then failure) is mitigated by limits but throughput is still an open alpha blocker; DWG save drops unmodelled data; never verified in AutoCAD; no real-file corpus
No CI runs the Rust tests on pull requests (S1) despite the never-crash architecture; project self-scores stability 35% with 27 of 37 open issues on core paths
No autosave in the web build; autosave is DXF not DWG; 10-minute default window of loss (no command journal)
WBLOCK copies the source's entire symbol table and writes non-atomically; dimension associativity is always dropped on paste/insert/xref import
docpath check is lexical only: symlinks, junctions and mapped drives can still reach another computer

genesis_relevant_findings.finding: Keep CADCraft's stored-path policy (craft-docpath: local or own-share only, refusals become statuses) and the bare-file-name-beside-host fallback - together they make a folder-shaped project relocatable. Change: add a project manifest beside the drawings listing every reference (xref, data link, underlay, font, template, plot style) with project-relative path, content hash, size, mtime and role; 'package/eTransmit' becomes copy-by-manifest instead of re-implementing eTransmit, which the project's gaps list (row F23) estimates at 40–70 hours. Persist xref status (CADCraft loses Unloaded) and the found-at path. Keep a .bak/previous version beside the atomic tmp+rename save, and make WBLOCK prune definitions like the clipboard does.

genesis_relevant_findings.finding: Keep the per-reference status enum with a human reason (Loaded/Unloaded/Not Found/Unresolved(reason)/Unreferenced), computed at open and reload and coloured in the palette, and the rule that a bad reference never blocks opening. Change: add one linkcheck command that walks the manifest (xrefs, nested xrefs, data links, underlays) and reports found/missing/refused/changed-since-load using a hash or mtime+size recorded at load (CADCraft records neither); add a file watcher so a modified xref raises a reload notice (CADCraft has none); decide explicitly whether to canonicalise symlinks before the lexical docpath check.
genesis_relevant_findings.evidence: xref/load.rs Outcome/Missing; ui-egui/src/xrefs.rs status colouring; grep notify/watch in engine and ui: none; craft-docpath docs caveat on symlinks

genesis_relevant_findings.finding: Keep the copy-on-write EntityStore (Arc chunks of 1024, sharded handle index): snapshots, undo, autosave and spatial caches are pointer copies, and it is the natural substrate for sharing a loaded reference between host, palette and caches without copying. Change: CADCraft re-reads and re-imports the whole referenced file on every Reload and loads xrefs synchronously after OPEN; Genesis should keep a process-wide parsed-reference cache keyed by (canonical path, size, mtime, hash), load references on a worker like OPEN's read_file/finish_open split, give each reference its own R-tree so pick/snap through a reference is logarithmic, and consider viewport-extent demand loading for large site bases. Keep every cap (files, bytes, objects, depth 16, cycle chain).
genesis_relevant_findings.evidence: crates/doc/src/store.rs; crates/engine/src/spatial.rs; cmd/file.rs read_file/finish_open; xref.rs after_open; load.rs caps

genesis_relevant_findings.finding: Keep the merge rules verbatim: existing named definitions in the target win, anonymous * blocks get fresh generated names, nested blocks and record-to-record dependencies (layer->linetype, dimstyle->textstyle) travel with the objects, new handles, source drawing uid tracked for Paste-to-original. CADCraft implements this three times (clipboard, insert-from-file, import); Genesis should have one merge_definitions used by paste, insert, import, bind and packaging. Change: add a stable per-object GUID so re-pasting the same source object is an idempotent update, return a merge report (kept/renamed/dropped) as the command result for users and agents, and remap handles to preserve dimension associativity when both ends were copied (CADCraft always drops it). Keep DXF text as the cross-process clipboard format.

Keep everything: deny lints for unwrap/expect/panic plus forbid(unsafe), Result everywhere, catch_unwind at every boundary (command, interactive step, prompt/preview, open, file read, DWG bridge, LISP, render thread) with restore from the pre-command Arc<Drawing>, non-finite refusal, the hostile_* test convention plus a cross-command hostile_params_never_panic, caps on every input-sized loop, background autosave with lock files and tmp+rename, immediate autosave on GPU fault, GPU errors captured by callbacks. Add what CADCraft lacks: a CI gate running the full check on every PR (this missing CI gate, gaps list row S1, is why the project rates its own stability 35% despite the architecture), an append-only command journal per drawing so recovery replays to the last action rather than the last 10-minute autosave, web autosave (IndexedDB), a DWG path that does not inflate 6x into DXF text (#57 was the first crash-adjacent failure users reported; the upstream tracker now holds about 42 issues matching 'crash', including GPU startup failures and an xref re-path crash) (reconciled after the fact-check and critique, 2026-10-21), reader fuzzing, and opt-in crash/hang telemetry so 'zero crashes' is measurable.

key_claims.claim: An xref is a Block with xref_path saved exactly as given; its objects are loaded from the referenced file's model space at open and on Reload and never saved with the host; xref_status is session-only

key_claims.claim: Stored paths are followed only on this computer or the drawing's own network share; UNC paths to other hosts, file://host URLs, device paths and URL schemes are refused with a reason and treated like a missing file
A missing xref leaves an empty block with status Not Found, the host opens, and the reference survives a save; a file later placed beside the host is found by name
Host overrides on xref layers survive save and reopen in both DXF and DWG

Nested xrefs load to at most 16 levels, overlays are not nested, circular references are detected by a canonical-path chain, and loads are capped at 4M objects / 1000 files / 512 MiB per file / 1 GiB total
Table data links read CSV/TSV only (8 MiB), with no Excel, no write-back and no web support, and travel as CADCraft xdata rather than AutoCAD DATALINK objects

Clipboard copies carry the layers, linetypes, styles and nested blocks they need; on paste the target's existing definitions win, anonymous blocks are renamed, objects get new handles and dimension associativity is dropped; cross-window transfer uses DXF text on the OS clipboard (50,000-object cap)

Autosave writes DXF every SAVETIME minutes (default 10) on a background thread with per-instance names and lock-file heartbeats; a GPU error or device loss triggers an immediate autosave; the web build has no autosave
Session::execute, interactive command steps, OPEN, the DWG bridge, LISP and the render thread all run under catch_unwind; an escaped panic restores the drawing and reports an internal error

A 9.9 MB AutoCAD 2010 DWG took about 1 min 50 s and 1.1 GB of memory before failing with 'file too large' on CADCraft 0.3.0; limits now stop runaway conversions early but throughput remains an alpha blocker
No CI runs the Rust test suite on pull requests; the project self-scores stability at 35%
No project container, eTransmit, Sheet Set Manager, Reference Manager or .bak backup exists; SAVE is atomic via tmp+rename
